  "text": "The woman at the alterations shop laid Ruth's coat across the table.

“Both sleeves?”

“Just the lining. My hand keeps going through.”

She turned one sleeve inside out. Pale fabric hung loose at the wrist.

“I can patch it, but it won't match.”

“No one sees it.”

“You do.”

Ruth looked at the rolls of thread arranged above the sewing machine.

“Something close, then.”

The woman opened a drawer and brought out three folded pieces. Ruth chose the grey.

“That's stronger,” the woman said.

Outside, a delivery driver was trying the door of the empty shop next door. He checked his phone, then tried again.

“Anything else while it's here?”

Ruth felt for the lower button.

“This one's loose.”

The woman bent over it.

“Different from the others.”

“My husband did that.”

“I've probably got a better match.”

“He took it off his own coat.”

The woman let the button fall against the wool.

“I'll tighten it.”

She wrote Ruth's name on a paper tag and looped it through a buttonhole.

“Thursday afternoon?”

“That should be fine.”

Ruth emptied the pockets: gloves, a receipt, two wrapped peppermints. She put everything into her handbag except the receipt, which she asked the woman to throw away.

At the door, she reached for the collar she was no longer wearing.

“Cold out?” the woman asked.

“A bit.”

“I can do Wednesday.”

“Thursday's fine. I've another one at home.”

Ruth fastened the top button of her cardigan before stepping outside."
